items.excerpt: A new optical-illusion typeface is engineered to be unreadable to AI/OCR systems while staying legible to humans — a craft-led designer pushback against machines scraping and reinterpreting visual work.

Veteran concept artist Daniel Porto argues AI has amplified rather than replaced his 20 years of craft, with creative vision and direction — not the tool — becoming the real competitive advantage in an AI-assisted workflow.
Argues generative AI is driving the first major shift in software interaction models in years, and asks whether designers are ready to invent the new patterns that go beyond chat boxes and prompts.
A design-AX essay: as AI absorbs execution work, design shifts from a craft function into the operating logic of the whole organisation, reshaping how design teams are structured and how they work.
A counter-narrative arguing users are fatigued by AI features bolted onto every product, and what that backlash means for how designers should — and shouldn't — integrate AI into real experiences.

DEVELOP3D interviews Novineer CEO Ali Tamijani on the startup's AI-driven reverse engineering that turns smartphone photos into optimised 3D models for additive-manufacturing and generative product design.

Designer channel Build Great Products ranks the major 2026 AI design tools — Figma, Anthropic's Claude Design and Google Stitch — testing each on the same brief to see which actually fits real product-design workflows.
